module: GE extension `core_vehicle_manager`: GE-side vehicle loader. When the engine creates a vehicle object, it calls `_spawnCCallback`: loads the materials from the model folder, builds the config (core_vehicle_partmgmt.buildConfigFromString), runs stage 1 of the jbeam loader (jbeam/loader), finishes the meshes, notifies the UI (VehicleChange), makes the player enter if autoEnterVehicle, then sends the physics data to the vehicle (spawnPhysics). Keeps for each vehicle its "bundle" (vdata = jbeam data, config, ioCtx...) accessible through getVehicleData, and applies paint changes live.
usage:
local d = core_vehicle_manager.getVehicleData(be:getPlayerVehicleID(0))
print(d.vehicleDirectory, d.model, d.config.partConfigFilename)
dump(d.vdata.nodes[0].pos)
-- paints by name
core_vehicle_manager.setVehicleColorsNames(vehId, {'Black', 'White', 'Red'})
notes: getVehicleData(id) returns the "bundle" of vehicles[id]: a table with at least vdata, config, ioCtx, vehicleDirectory, model, mainPartName, activePlayer (fields read elsewhere in the code; the exact detail comes from jbeam/loader).

BUG: setVehicleColorsNames tests `vehicle.color == vehicle.colorPalette0 == vehicle.colorPalette1`, which compares a boolean to a color and is always false: the `optional` parameter therefore never protects anything.

Probable BUG: in _spawnCCallback, `additionalVehicleData and not additionalDataId or additionalDataId == objID` mixes and/or without parentheses; if additionalDataId is nil, the condition is true when additionalVehicleData exists (intended) but also true if additionalDataId == objID.
setVehiclePaintsNames is an alias of setVehicleColorsNames.

The "Vehicle Manager" editor (onEditorGui) is marked obsolete in the code: it only displays the -debugVehicleLoading command-line argument to use instead. The -profileVehicleLoading and -debugVehicleLoading arguments are read when the module loads.
onUpdate calls spawn.clearCache() every frame (placement cache of spawn.lua).

autoSpawnPhysics.desc: true by default; if false, physics is not sent to the vehicle after loading (spawnPhysicsForVehicle must be called by hand). Also disabled for a vehicle whose NoPhysics == 'true'.

getDebug.desc: Indicates whether the vehicle loading debug mode is active.

setDebug.desc: Enables/disables loading debug (passed in additionalVehicleData.debugEnabled) and notifies the UI (guihook debugSpawnChanged).

queueAdditionalVehicleData.desc: Prepares a table of additional data that will be added to the config of the next loaded vehicle (config.additionalVehicleData, removed afterwards). Called by core_vehicles on spawn/replacement.

vehId.desc: if given, only this vehicle will receive the data

spawnPhysicsForVehicle.desc: Sends the vehicle (vehicleObj:spawnPhysics) its encoded physics data (vdata + config); sends an empty packet if the bundle is absent.

vehicleBundle.desc: bundle to send (default: the stored one)

_spawnCCallback.desc: Called by the C++ engine when a vehicle object is created or reloaded: loads materials, config and jbeam (stage 1), notifies, makes the player enter (autoEnterVehicle / autoEnterVehiclePlayer) and starts the physics. Emits the onSpawnCCallback(objID) hook and calls vehicleSpawned(objID).

reloading.desc: true on a reload (not used in the code)

getVehicleData.desc: Data bundle of a vehicle (jbeam vdata, config, ioCtx...).

returns.desc: bundle; nil if the vehicle is unknown

liveUpdateVehicleColors.desc: Changes the paint of a slot on the vehicle object (color, colorPalette0, colorPalette1 + metallic data) without respawn, then emits onVehicleColorChanged(objID, index, paint). Does nothing if the vehicle has no config.paints.

setVehicleColorsNames.desc: Applies up to 3 named paints (from model.paints) to a vehicle, live.

optional.desc: if non-nil, was meant to cancel the action when the vehicle's 3 colors are identical (ineffective, see notes)

toggleModifyKey.desc: Shows/hides the vehicle in-place editing window (core_vehicle_inplaceEdit).

reloadVehicle.desc: Reloads a player's vehicle: notifies core_vehicles.reloadVehicle then be:reloadVehicle(playerId).

onVehicleSwitched.desc: Hook: the player changes vehicle. Updates activePlayer of the bundles and releases the clutch (input.event('clutch', 0, 0)) of the old vehicle.

onDespawnObject.desc: Hook: a vehicle object is removed. Forgets its bundle unless it is a reload (isReloading true).

onClientEndMission.desc: Hook: end of the level; invalidates the loaded materials cache.

onFileChanged.desc: Hook: a file changed. Notifies jbeam/io for .jbeam files and invalidates the materials cache of a vehicle folder if a .materials.json changes there.

onUpdate.desc: Per-frame hook: empties the placement cache of spawn.lua.

onSerialize.desc: Hook: encodes (lpack) the bundles before a Lua reload.

onDeserialized.desc: Hook: restores the bundles encoded by onSerialize.

onEditorInitialized.desc: Editor hook: registers the obsolete "Vehicle Manager" window.

onEditorGui.desc: Editor hook: displays an obsolescence message recommending -debugVehicleLoading.
